subject: Anatomy
fact: The median nerve passes through the carpal tunnel, while its palmar cutaneous branch travels superficial to the flexor retinaculum.

subject: Anatomy
fact: The ulnar nerve passes posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus, making it vulnerable at the elbow.

subject: Anatomy
fact: The common fibular nerve winds around the neck of the fibula and is vulnerable to injury at that site.

subject: Anatomy
fact: The phrenic nerve runs anterior to the root of the lung, while the vagus nerve runs posterior to it.

subject: Anatomy
fact: The portal vein is formed mainly by the union of the superior mesenteric and splenic veins.

subject: Physiology
fact: The sinoatrial node is the normal pacemaker because it has the highest spontaneous firing rate in the heart.

subject: Physiology
fact: Cardiac output equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume.

subject: Physiology
fact: Most carbon dioxide in blood is transported as bicarbonate rather than as dissolved gas.

subject: Physiology
fact: Pulmonary surfactant lowers alveolar surface tension and helps prevent alveolar collapse.

subject: Physiology
fact: The kidneys help regulate acid-base balance by reabsorbing bicarbonate and excreting hydrogen ions.

subject: Biochemistry
fact: Glycolysis occurs in the cytosol and converts glucose to pyruvate while generating ATP and NADH.

subject: Biochemistry
fact: The citric acid cycle occurs mainly in the mitochondrial matrix.

subject: Biochemistry
fact: Vitamin B12 deficiency can cause megaloblastic anemia together with neurologic abnormalities.

subject: Biochemistry
fact: Vitamin C is required for hydroxylation reactions involved in collagen synthesis.

subject: Biochemistry
fact: Competitive inhibition usually increases apparent Km without changing Vmax.

subject: Pathology
fact: Coagulative necrosis is typical of ischemic injury in most solid organs except the brain.

subject: Pathology
fact: Liquefactive necrosis is classically seen in brain infarcts and many bacterial abscesses.

subject: Pathology
fact: Neutrophils are usually the predominant cells in early acute inflammation.

subject: Pathology
fact: Iron deficiency anemia is typically microcytic and hypochromic.

subject: Pathology
fact: Nephrotic syndrome is characterized by heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and often hyperlipidemia.

subject: Pharmacology
fact: Atropine is a competitive antagonist at muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.

subject: Pharmacology
fact: ACE inhibitors reduce angiotensin II formation and also decrease bradykinin breakdown.

subject: Pharmacology
fact: Loop diuretics inhibit the sodium-potassium-2 chloride cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.

subject: Pharmacology
fact: Beta-lactam antibiotics inhibit bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins.

subject: Pharmacology
fact: Benzodiazepines enhance the effect of GABA at GABA-A receptors.

subject: Microbiology
fact: Staphylococcus aureus is catalase-positive and coagulase-positive.

subject: Microbiology
fact: Streptococcus pyogenes is a group A beta-hemolytic streptococcus.

subject: Microbiology
fact: Mycobacteria are acid-fast because of lipid-rich mycolic acids in their cell walls.

subject: Microbiology
fact: Influenza viruses have segmented RNA genomes, which allows reassortment.

subject: Microbiology
fact: IgM is usually the first antibody class produced during a primary immune response.

subject: Community Medicine
fact: Incidence measures new cases occurring in a population over a specified period.

subject: Community Medicine
fact: Prevalence measures how much disease exists in a population at a particular time or over a period.

subject: Community Medicine
fact: Positive predictive value generally increases as disease prevalence increases, assuming test sensitivity and specificity stay the same.

subject: Community Medicine
fact: Primary prevention aims to prevent disease before it occurs.

subject: Community Medicine
fact: Case-control studies typically begin with outcome status and then assess previous exposures.

subject: Medicine
fact: Atrial fibrillation produces an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm.

subject: Medicine
fact: Asthma is characterized by variable airflow obstruction and airway hyperresponsiveness.

subject: Medicine
fact: Type 1 diabetes mellitus results from autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells.

subject: Medicine
fact: An upper motor neuron lesion commonly causes weakness with increased tone and hyperreflexia below the lesion.

subject: Medicine
fact: Rheumatoid arthritis commonly affects small joints symmetrically and is associated with prolonged morning stiffness.

subject: Surgery
fact: A strangulated hernia has compromised blood supply and requires urgent surgical assessment.

subject: Surgery
fact: Appendicitis classically begins with vague periumbilical pain that later localizes to the right lower quadrant.

subject: Surgery
fact: Gallstones can obstruct the cystic duct and cause acute cholecystitis.

subject: Surgery
fact: Initial trauma assessment prioritizes airway, breathing, circulation, disability, and exposure.

subject: Surgery
fact: Acute limb ischemia is classically remembered by the six Ps: pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, and poikilothermia.

subject: Pediatrics
fact: Physiologic jaundice in newborns is related partly to increased bilirubin production and immature hepatic conjugation.

subject: Pediatrics
fact: Developmental assessment considers gross motor, fine motor, language, and social domains.

subject: Pediatrics
fact: Bronchiolitis most often affects infants and is commonly caused by respiratory syncytial virus.

subject: Pediatrics
fact: Growth in children is best assessed by plotting measurements serially on age- and sex-appropriate growth charts.

subject: Pediatrics
fact: Major public-health organizations recommend exclusive breastfeeding for about the first six months of life.

subject: Obstetrics & Gynecology
fact: Human chorionic gonadotropin is produced mainly by syncytiotrophoblasts in early pregnancy.

subject: Obstetrics & Gynecology
fact: Preeclampsia is new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation with proteinuria or other evidence of maternal organ dysfunction.

subject: Obstetrics & Gynecology
fact: Ovulation is triggered by the mid-cycle luteinizing hormone surge.

subject: Obstetrics & Gynecology
fact: The ampullary portion of the fallopian tube is the most common site of ectopic pregnancy.

subject: Obstetrics & Gynecology
fact: FSH stimulates granulosa cells, while LH stimulates theca cells in the ovarian follicle.

subject: ENT
fact: The middle ear communicates with the nasopharynx through the auditory tube.

subject: ENT
fact: Conductive hearing loss results from impaired transmission of sound through the external or middle ear.

subject: ENT
fact: The recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies most intrinsic muscles of the larynx.

subject: ENT
fact: Kiesselbach area on the anterior nasal septum is a common site of epistaxis.

subject: Ophthalmology
fact: The optic nerve is cranial nerve II and carries visual information from the retina to the brain.

subject: Ophthalmology
fact: Glaucoma is a progressive optic neuropathy involving retinal ganglion cell loss, often associated with elevated intraocular pressure.

subject: Ophthalmology
fact: A cataract is an opacity of the crystalline lens that can reduce visual acuity.

subject: Ophthalmology
fact: The macula is responsible for high-acuity central vision.

subject: Dermatology
fact: The epidermis is avascular and receives nutrients by diffusion from the underlying dermis.

subject: Dermatology
fact: Psoriasis commonly produces well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale.

subject: Dermatology
fact: Dermatophytes infect keratinized tissues such as skin, hair, and nails.

subject: Dermatology
fact: Melanocytes synthesize melanin and transfer melanosomes to keratinocytes.

subject: Psychiatry
fact: Major depressive episodes involve persistent low mood or loss of interest together with other cognitive and physical symptoms.

subject: Psychiatry
fact: Schizophrenia can involve positive symptoms, negative symptoms, and cognitive impairment.

subject: Psychiatry
fact: Panic attacks are episodes of intense fear accompanied by prominent physical and cognitive symptoms.

subject: Psychiatry
fact: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are widely used first-line treatments for several depressive and anxiety disorders.

subject: Radiology
fact: Air appears dark on a plain radiograph because it attenuates fewer X-rays than soft tissue or bone.

subject: Radiology
fact: CT uses X-rays to create cross-sectional images and is widely used for rapid assessment of acute conditions.

subject: Radiology
fact: MRI does not use ionizing radiation and provides excellent soft-tissue contrast.

subject: Radiology
fact: Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves and provides real-time imaging without ionizing radiation.

subject: Forensic Medicine
fact: Fingerprints are highly individual and remain an important method of personal identification.

subject: Forensic Medicine
fact: Accurate contemporaneous documentation is essential in medicolegal practice.

subject: Forensic Medicine
fact: Valid consent requires capacity, adequate information, and voluntariness.

subject: Orthopedics
fact: Fracture healing progresses through stages that include hematoma formation, callus formation, and remodeling.

subject: Orthopedics
fact: Intracapsular fractures of the femoral neck can compromise the blood supply to the femoral head.

subject: Orthopedics
fact: The intervertebral disc consists of an outer annulus fibrosus and an inner nucleus pulposus.

subject: Orthopedics
fact: A posterior hip dislocation can injure the sciatic nerve.

subject: Anesthesiology
fact: Pre-anesthetic airway assessment helps identify features associated with difficult ventilation or intubation.

subject: Anesthesiology
fact: Local anesthetics block voltage-gated sodium channels and prevent propagation of action potentials.

subject: Emergency Medicine
fact: High-quality chest compressions are a core component of cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

subject: Emergency Medicine
fact: Shock is a state of inadequate tissue perfusion and may be hypovolemic, distributive, cardiogenic, or obstructive.

subject: Anatomy
fact: Broca area is classically located in the dominant inferior frontal gyrus and is involved in motor speech production.

subject: Physiology
fact: Erythropoietin is produced mainly by peritubular interstitial cells in the kidney in response to hypoxia.

subject: Biochemistry
fact: Albumin is the major plasma protein contributing to plasma oncotic pressure.

subject: Pathology
fact: Metastasis is a defining feature of malignant tumors.

subject: Pharmacology
fact: Metformin reduces hepatic glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity.

subject: Microbiology
fact: Malaria is transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes carrying Plasmodium parasites.

subject: Medicine
fact: Portal hypertension can lead to esophageal varices, splenomegaly, and ascites.

subject: Surgery
fact: Most lymphatic drainage of the breast is to the axillary lymph nodes.

subject: Pediatrics
fact: A ventricular septal defect is one of the most common congenital heart defects.

subject: Obstetrics & Gynecology
fact: The placenta acts as the interface for exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste products between maternal and fetal circulations.
